root_causes.description: An abort injected at the payment HTTP/gRPC boundary prevents checkout's outbound call to payment from ever completing, so checkout blocks until its 10s deadline and the delay propagates to frontend. Because the abort occurs at the boundary, payment emits no completed or errored server span, leaving its own error_rate and latency metrics normal while its observed request rate collapses.

evidence.expected_baseline: checkout p99 well under 1000 ms; pinned exactly at the 10s gRPC deadline
frontend p99 < 1000 ms; blocked on the checkout→payment path
normal payment latency; no server-side latency inflation, consistent with abort at boundary rather than slow processing
expected >0 if payment itself errored; zero confirms the failure is at the boundary (no completed/errored server span)

evidence.observed_value: payment request_rate mean=0.010, p50=0.000, p95=0.038, max=0.038
evidence.expected_baseline: steady payment request_rate matching checkout volume; near-zero indicates checkout→payment calls are not reaching/completing at payment
if payment returned an error span, errored checkout traces would be present; absence is consistent with abort at boundary
no application-level error logs; the block is a deadline/timeout rather than a handled error

evidence.observed_value: only routine 'Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource' (count=1) events
evidence.expected_baseline: no OOMKilled/BackOff/FailedMount; rules out pod_crash/memory_stress as the cause

root_causes.description: Alternative interpretation: a network partition isolating the payment pods prevents checkout's outbound gRPC call from completing, producing the same 10s-deadline block at checkout while payment emits no server spans and its request rate collapses.

evidence.expected_baseline: steady payment request_rate matching checkout volume; near-zero is consistent with a connectivity break to payment

evidence.observed_value: checkout p99=10000.0 ms blocked at deadline
evidence.expected_baseline: checkout p99 < 1000 ms; inability to reach payment would block the chain to the deadline

evidence.observed_value: only routine 'Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource' (count=1) events, no partition/network events logged
evidence.expected_baseline: no evidence of a NetworkPolicy or partition change captured in pod events during the window

root_causes.description: Alternative interpretation: the fault resides at checkout's egress dependency to payment, where checkout waits on an unresponsive downstream; the near-zero payment request rate and pinned 10s checkout latency are equally consistent with a downstream dependency that never responds.

evidence.observed_value: checkout p99=10000.0 ms at the 10s deadline

evidence.expected_baseline: unhandled downstream dependency failure would surface as slow/errored checkout traces
a hard downstream failure would typically raise checkout server error spans; zero suggests deadline-bound blocking rather than explicit errors

remediation_steps: Disable / roll back the flagd flag injecting the http_abort fault on the payment service to restore normal responses for checkout's outbound call.
Restart the payment deployment pods to clear any stuck/aborted connection state and re-establish checkout→payment gRPC channels.
Verify recovery by confirming checkout p99 latency returns below ~1000 ms and payment request_rate recovers to checkout-matched volume.
If the abort persists, inspect NetworkPolicy/partition injection isolating payment pods in namespace otel-demo and remove/roll back the partition to restore checkout→payment connectivity.
